key_insight: A physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order modeling framework enables aerodynamic shape optimization of unsteady flapping wings while targeting greater stability and lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make optimization of thrust and propulsive efficiency more practical for complex flapping-wing designs.
method: Replace large-scale PDE-constrained optimization with reduced-order-model-constrained optimization.
Project optimization into system dynamics optimization in Hilbert space to improve sensitivity stability.
Apply the framework to 2D wing-section shape optimization and test it on a 3D flapping wing.
evidence_signal: For a 2D flapping wing section at Re = 2,400 with chaotic flow structures, the abstract reports gains of 37% in time-averaged thrust and 40% in propulsive efficiency, plus a 3D test.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational savings or 3D performance gains, leaving scalability and broader applicability to be assessed.
paper_title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
